http-request.regex:
^(GET|POST|HEAD) /[a-zA-Z0-9/._?=&%-]* HTTP/1\.1
Host: [a-z0-9.-]+
User-Agent: Mozilla/5\.0 \([a-zA-Z0-9;: .()/_-]+\)
Accept: [a-zA-Z0-9/*,;= .+-]+
Accept-Language: [a-z,;=0-9. -]+

$
http-request.hybrid_regex:
^POST /[a-zA-Z0-9/._?=&%-]* HTTP/1\.1
Host: [a-z0-9.-]+
User-Agent: Mozilla/5\.0 \([a-zA-Z0-9;: .()/_-]+\)
Accept: [a-zA-Z0-9/*,;= .+-]+
Accept-Language: [a-z,;=0-9. -]+
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

$
http-request.description: HTTP request headers; format-mode records are 200-700 bytes. Hybrid uses a 200-byte POST header and a chunked encrypted body.

http-response.regex:
^HTTP/1\.1 (200 OK|302 Found|304 Not Modified|404 Not Found)
Server: [a-zA-Z0-9/. ()_-]+
Content-Type: [a-zA-Z0-9/;=. +-]+
Content-Length: 0
ETag: "[a-zA-Z0-9]+"
Set-Cookie: [a-zA-Z0-9]+=[a-zA-Z0-9%_-]+; Path=/

$
http-response.hybrid_regex:
^HTTP/1\.1 (200 OK|302 Found|404 Not Found)
Server: [a-zA-Z0-9/. ()_-]+
Content-Type: [a-zA-Z0-9/;=. +-]+
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
ETag: "[a-zA-Z0-9]+"
Set-Cookie: [a-zA-Z0-9]+=[a-zA-Z0-9%_-]+; Path=/

$
http-response.description: HTTP response headers with an empty body in format mode (200-700 bytes). Hybrid uses a 200-byte header and a chunked encrypted body.

ftp-request.description: FTP command shape with a CRLF terminator; 64-256 bytes per format-mode record.

ftp-response.description: FTP status code and generated reply text with a CRLF terminator; 64-256 bytes per format-mode record.

smtp-request.description: SMTP command shape with a CRLF terminator; 80-320 bytes per format-mode record.

smtp-response.description: SMTP status/text shape, including 250- continuation lines; 80-320 bytes per format-mode record.

sip-request.regex:
^(INVITE|REGISTER|ACK|BYE|OPTIONS) sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+ SIP/2\.0
Via: SIP/2\.0/TCP [a-z0-9.-]+;branch=z9hG4bK[a-zA-Z0-9]+
From: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>;tag=[a-zA-Z0-9]+
To: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>
Call-ID: [a-zA-Z0-9]+@[a-z0-9.-]+
CSeq: [0-9]+ (INVITE|REGISTER|ACK|BYE|OPTIONS)
Content-Length: 0

$
sip-request.description: SIP request shape with Via, From, To, Call-ID, CSeq, and an empty body; 300-800 bytes per format-mode record.

sip-response.regex:
^SIP/2\.0 (100 Trying|180 Ringing|200 OK|404 Not Found)
Via: SIP/2\.0/TCP [a-z0-9.-]+;branch=z9hG4bK[a-zA-Z0-9]+
From: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>;tag=[a-zA-Z0-9]+
To: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>
Call-ID: [a-zA-Z0-9]+@[a-z0-9.-]+
CSeq: [0-9]+ (INVITE|REGISTER|ACK|BYE|OPTIONS)
Content-Length: 0

$
sip-response.description: SIP response shape with Via, From, To, Call-ID, CSeq, and an empty body; 300-800 bytes per format-mode record.

dns-request.description: DNS-over-TCP query shape: external two-byte prefix and one A/AAAA question; 90-272 wire bytes, with QNAME 72-254 bytes.

dns-response.description: DNS-over-TCP reply shape: external two-byte prefix, one question, and one A answer pointing to that question; 90-272 wire bytes.
